findings_to_judge.finding: On the 2026-06-08 Q1 call Duluth's CFO said 'For the IEEPA tariffs of approximately $12 million paid last year, we have applied for refunds but have not included any potential benefit in the results this quarter or in the full year guidance' - a windfall equal to ~8.7% of the $138M market cap and ~$0.32/share that is carried at zero in the affirmed FY2026 adjusted-EBITDA guide of $28-32M and in the single sell-side estimate of $(0.05), and Duluth's Q2 ended 2026-08-02, i.e. inside the window in which the rest of retail actually booked these refunds.
